title: I made it easier to see trading news that actually matters. Free!
author: KimOnMacro
selftext:
Most traders use AI search or X to check trading news.

But there's 2 main problems with this:

**1. AI search: News takes time to appear and can confidently state old news. Still good for getting general trend summaries or big events etc** 

**2. X: Fast but each individual post doesnt tie back into whats actually going on so youre manually connecting dots.** 

**So I went and talked to the Financial Juice team and got their breaking news feed built directly into my app!**   
  
My app already gives a market summary from all my data sources, and remembers the current state so each breaking news that comes in updates the memory for context when summarising the market environment for you. (although Ive put a filter to only show headlines in the suummary if it's relevant enough to move the current market)  


But if you like seeing all the headlines yourself, you can still browse the raw feed on the side which autotags to relevant assets. E.g. on my screenshot you can see theres a headline of China buying $289B in forex. This autotags to AUD as australian economy is strongly correlated with chinese buying power for Australias metal ores etc. (This doesn't shift the bias though, as current AUDUSD is mostly driven by consecutive US print results)

  
**Its free to use here:**  
[https://echelonedgeai.com/](https://echelonedgeai.com/) 

My app is in free beta but you can still get breaking news for free anyway as famous X accounts like financial juice or walter bloomberg post a lot. FX street also gives great market summaries too that you can look over for context.   


The feedback here has been really useful in the past, so let me know what I'm missing this time. Appreciate it!

replies.body: Free beta until Sep 18! Although users have recently asked for a limited freemium to have more time to play around with the app. On the fence for that one but if I get more feedback to improve, Will def consider it :)

replies.author: fomoz
replies.body: But your main news source is free. What does that say about the usefulness of your app vs the price? Even TradingView data starts at line $10 per month and has a free forever tier as well.

replies.author: KimOnMacro
replies.body:
Haha yeah, some of the sources I use aren't exactly free 😂   
But if you're just after a news feed, then 100% not worth it!  
  
The point is bringing live data, prices, positioning, macro and breaking news together and showing what it actually means for the trade.

replies.author: fomoz
replies.body:
But TradingView already has news. And you're just using their Advanced Charts libary, I think.

Your app is maybe $1 to $3 if it really has a unique value prop. Anyway, good luck.

replies.author: fomoz
replies.body: By the way, putting TradingView Advanced Charts behind a paywall violates their free license terms. If they notify you of the breach and you don’t fix it within 10 days, the agreement allows them to seek $50,000 in liquidated damages per proven breach.

comments.author: MichaellBrownnn
comments.body: But as far as I understand, news isn’t always that useful

replies.author: KimOnMacro
replies.body: Exactly! Sorry, my description probably made it sound like I just built a breaking newsfeed. The idea is more that the app has a “market memory” of what’s already driving the asset, so when new information comes in it can be judged against that existing context. A hawkish central bank headline might sound bullish, but if multiple hikes are already priced in and the existing macro/positioning picture hasn't changed, it doesn't necessarily shift the bias.

comments.author: DifficultyOwn3050
comments.body:
The context memory part is what caught my attention  breaking headline by itself isnt always useful its the connection to what the market was already doing that makes it actionable

How are you deciding which headlines are actually significant enough to update the market bias?

replies.author: KimOnMacro
replies.body:
Thank you for your question! This is actually one of the areas I've been fine tuning quite a bit, so I appreciate you asking.

I roughly split news into 3 tiers:  
Tier 1 is something that can genuinely change the macro picture, like a surprise rate decision or major economic print.  
Tier 2 supports or weakens something that's already driving the market, so it can influence the bias depending on the existing context.  
Tier 3 is relevant/interesting but probably doesn't change the current story. It stays in the feed, but doesn't touch the verdict.  
  
Then there's a bunch of extra checks around whether it's actually new, already priced in, a duplicate, contradicts the existing market behaviour, and whether other markets are confirming it.

Still in the process of tweaks and sadly do spot data slip throughs occasionally but working my best to make it as accurate as possible!

replies.author: DifficultyOwn3050
replies.body: makes sense how the system handles conflicting signals across different markets.?

replies.author: KimOnMacro
replies.body: I've currentl designed it so it weighs the bullish vs bearish factors alongside the 3 tiers. Then based on other factors such as recency and timeframe the weighting will change. So one major bearish signal can outweigh several weaker bullish ones. Unfortunately this is the part that I had the biggest trouble with in terms of data slip throughs but hoping to really improve the accuracy over the next month.
